title: Enterprise onboarding: integration, escalation, known issues, health checks & QBR playbook
author: Avery Martinez
content:
Summary

This playbook consolidates the enterprise onboarding checklist and operational guidance we use for: initial integration, ongoing health checks, QBR preparation, and escalation handling. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Technical Account Managers (TAMs), DevOps/Platform, and SREs supporting enterprise customers.

Purpose

- Provide a single reference for onboarding milestones, integration prerequisites, escalation flows, and known issues/workarounds.
- Reduce time-to-production by standardizing steps and ownership.
- Ensure consistent operational posture and QBR artefacts for long-term retention.

Scope

Applies to enterprise customers (contract value > $50k ARR) undergoing: Hosted API onboarding, Dedicated reservation, or Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments. Excludes exploratory POCs under the PLG free tier unless upgraded to enterprise support.

Roles & responsibilities

- Customer Success (Owner): onboarding project manager, QBR cadence, customer communications.
- TAM / Solutions Engineer: technical integration, API contract validation, sample prompts & evals.
- Eng SRE / Platform: capacity provision, routing policies, monitoring & alerting.
- Support (L1/L2): first-line triage for incidents, known-issues lookup.
- Escalation on-call (L3): long-term fixes, mitigations, and code/infra changes.

Onboarding checklist (milestones)

1. Pre-kickoff (CS)
   - Collect requirements: throughput, latency SLOs, data residency, compliance controls, and model preferences.
   - Share required artifacts: account IDs, IP allowlist CIDRs, KMS configuration, and SSO metadata.

2. Kickoff (week 0)
   - Stakeholder alignment: CS, TAM, customer infra, security.
   - Confirm environment: Hosted / Dedicated / Private, region(s), and baseline capacity.
   - Create project tracker and assign owners.

3. Integration (week 1–2)
   - API keys: generate test keys and validate with curl examples.
     Example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"rwkv-13b", "prompt":"Hello"}'
   - Network: confirm IP allowlist; if Private, validate VPN or Direct Connect.
   - Schema and tooling: confirm input/output schemas, function calling contracts, and streaming expectations.
   - Baseline usage tests: run 100 concurrent requests with representative prompt mix.

4. Validation & performance (week 2–3)
   - Latency: measure P50/P95 against agreed SLOs. Standard target: P95 < 250ms for short requests (<=512 tokens) on Dedicated.
   - Throughput: validate tokens/sec under steady load and peak bursts.
   - Cost model review: provide cost estimates using Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, cache, quantization).

5. Go‑live & runbook handoff (week 3–4)
   - Enable production keys, finalize rate limits, and set SLO dashboards.
   - Share runbooks: incident triage, rollback, and contact matrix.
   - Schedule first QBR at 30 days.

Integration guide (technical checklist)

- API compatibility: confirm model name/version and tokenizer mapping.
- Prefix caching: configure prefix cache TTL based on prompt reuse. Recommended TTL: 1h for microservices-heavy workloads.
- Batching: enable client-side batching for high throughput applications; target batch sizes of 8–32 depending on model and latency tolerance.
- Authentication: recommend short-lived tokens (rotate monthly) and integrate with SSO where possible.
- Observability hooks: add request-id header and pass-through for tracing.
  - Header: X-Request-ID: <uuid>
- Error handling: implement exponential backoff with jitter for 429/503 responses.

Escalation flow (incident severity definitions)

Severity levels
- Sev 1 (Critical): production outage affecting >50% customers or critical data loss. Response target: 15 min to acknowledge, 1 hour to mitigation plan.
- Sev 2 (High): degraded service that impacts key functionality for a subset of customers. Response target: 30 min acknowledge, 4 hour mitigation.
- Sev 3 (Medium): partial impact or performance degradation; longer-term fix tracked in ticket.
- Sev 4 (Low): cosmetic or minor bugs; handled in standard backlog.

Escalation steps (1–6)
1. L1 Support triage: collect logs, request-id, timestamp, customer-impact scope, and reproduce steps.
2. Apply known-workarounds (see Known Issues section).
3. If unresolved in 30 minutes (Sev1) or 4 hours (Sev2), escalate to L2 with detailed packet (attachments: raw logs, trace links, rate-limit metrics).
4. L2 troubleshooting: validate infra (node health, GPU memory), routing policies, and KV cache state.
5. Escalate to on-call L3 if code or infra remediation required; provide proposed mitigation steps and temporary workarounds.
6. Communicate status every 30 minutes (Sev1) / 2 hours (Sev2) to customer & CS until resolved.

Contact matrix

- Primary CS owner: CS_team@redwood.ai (include project tracker link).
- Support (L1): support@redwood.ai (ticket intake).
- On-call L3: PagerDuty (team: inference-runtime-oncall).

Known issues & workarounds

| ID | Symptom | Impact | Root cause (summary) | Short-term workaround | Owner |
|----|---------|--------|----------------------|-----------------------|-------|
| KI-101 | Intermittent 503s during burst traffic | Some requests fail under heavy burst | Burst queue overflow on autoscaler cooldown | Increase burst pool or stagger client retries with jitter; enable client-side batching | eng-sre |
| KI-114 | Tokenization mismatch on dev -> prod | Text truncation or misaligned output | Model tokenizer version mismatch between environments | Pin tokenizer version in deployment; run tokenizer-check tool (token-checker --model <name>) | eng-serving-runtime |
| KI-127 | Elevated P95 latency for >1k tokens | Slow tail latency for long-context requests | KV cache eviction and large attention costs | Use quantized model variant for long-context; enable prefix caching and limit max concurrent long-context requests | eng-platform |
| KI-139 | 429s returned during scheduled maintenance | Rate limiting on some tenants | Maintenance window misconfiguration | Notify customers in advance; apply maintenance header: X-Maintenance-Window | support |

Support process & ticket lifecycle

- Ticket intake: support@redwood.ai or customer portal. Include: customer name, tenant id, request-id(s), timestamps, and representative payload.
- Triage SLA: acknowledge within 1 business hour.
- Severity classification: applied by L1 using above definitions.
- Ticket routing: L1 -> L2 (TAM/SE) -> L3 (on-call) per escalation flow.
- Root cause analysis: for Sev1/Sev2 incidents, prepare a postmortem within 5 business days (see incident-postmortem-template).

Health checks & monitoring (daily / weekly / monthly)

Daily
- Check: SLO dashboard for error rate (target < 0.5% 5xx), request queue length, and GPU memory pressure.
- Run: smoke test suite (10 representative prompts) against production keys.

Weekly
- Review: Top 10 customers by token consumption, P95 latency trends, and cost anomalies.
- Validate: Cache hit ratio and batching efficiency metrics.

Monthly / QBR prep
- Compile: 30/60/90 day metrics: throughput, latency, error rates, cost per 1k tokens, and model quality regressions (linked evals).
- Action items: suggested Optimize recommendations (quantization, batching, cache TTL changes) and planned rollouts.
- Template items for QBR slides: executive summary, usage trends, incident summary (last 90 days), roadmap, and ask (capacity / feature requests).

Operational runbooks & links

- Incident runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-response (link)
- Capacity playbook: /confluence/eng-sre/capacity-planning
- Integration examples & templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates

Metrics & SLOs (examples)
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for Dedicated customers.
- Error rate: 5xx < 0.5% of requests measured per day.
- Latency: P95 < 250ms for short requests (<=512 tokens) on Dedicated; P95 < 800ms for long-context on Dedicated.

Post-onboarding checklist

- Confirm runbook access for customer ops team.
- Handover to TAM for ongoing QBR cadence.
- Schedule quarterly model-eval reviews (link to eval-harness) and cost optimization review.

Appendix: sample incident communication template

- Subject: [Sev1] Redwood Inference outage impacting <Customer> – <short summary>
- Body: timeframe, impact, immediate mitigation, next steps, ETA for full resolution, points of contact.

Revision history

- 2026-03-10: Created by Avery Martinez.
- 2026-06-01: Updated with new KI entries and revised SLO targets; reviewers: Samir Gupta, Talia Rivera, Ben O'Connor.

If you have questions or need this playbook adapted to a specific contract or private deployment, open a request with CS via the project tracker or contact the TAM assigned to the account.
